course_description: This course will focus on developing research knowledge and competencies in a teaching and learning setting. By the end of this course, students will be able to search and identify quality research as a form of professional learning, be able to read and critically understand research that can inform teaching practices and design a research project that evaluates teaching and learning with the aim to improve student learning. Further, the students will be asked to develop this plan by working with each other as professional colleagues, as well as engaging with professional teaching networks and the broader community.

learning_activities.topic: Wk 1 Lecture: What is Quality Research in Health, Sport Pedagogy and Education? Overarching Themes: What is research? How does research serve as a form of professional learning? What makes something 'quality' research? What are the different types of research? How can I find quality research? What are the roles of professional organisations in research? Learning outcomes: L02, L03, L06

Wk 1 Tutorial: Finding Quality Research in Health, Sport Pedagogy and Education Overarching Themes: Identify a topic of interest in health, sport pedagogy and education that is relevant to researchers and teaching professionals Find research that is relevant and credible for that topic Identify key journals and publication outlets in health, sport pedagogy and education Recognise different types of research sources, such as journal articles, books, reports and professional resources Make basic judgements about whether a research source is credible, relevant and useful for understanding or improving practice Investigate professional organisations and professional communities of practice that address quality practice in Health, Sport Pedagogy and Education Learning outcomes: L02, L03, L06

Wk 2 Lecture: How Research Questions Are Framed and Planned Overarching Themes: Explain how research is used to answer different kinds of questions Understand how a researcher's positionality influences the choices they make about research Identify and understand how different frameworks (e.g. positivist, constructivist, Aboriginal and Indigenous paradigms) shape how researchers frame, understand, and study a topic Identify common research genres (e.g. conversational inquiry, descriptive research, field-based inquiry) and specific research designs (e.g. interview studies, survey studies, practitioner enquiry) that are used to create an overarching plan for research Explain why different frameworks and research designs are suited to answering different research questions Learning outcomes: L03

Wk 2 Tutorial: Understanding the Choices Behind Research Overarching Themes: Identify a topic of interest in health, sport pedagogy and education that is relevant to researchers and teaching professionals Find research that is relevant and credible for that topic Describe the question, framework and design used in that research output Consider why a researcher or teaching professional may choose a particular framework or design for their inquiry Discuss how researcher positionality and choices shape what a study can show, explain or claim, and how this may inform teaching practice Learning outcomes: L03

Wk 3 Lecture: Qualitative Conversational Inquiry - Using Conversations to Understand Teaching, Learning and Experiences Overarching Themes: Explain why researchers and teaching professionals use conversational and interview-based inquiry in health, sport pedagogy and education Identify the kinds of questions conversational inquiry can help researchers and teaching professionals explore Understand how conversational inquiry may look different when shaped by different frameworks, such as positivist, constructivist and Aboriginal/Indigenous paradigms Identify different types of interviews and conversations, such as structured, semi-structured, unstructured and yarning-based conversations Explain how conversational inquiry can help researchers and teaching professionals understand experience, meaning, relationships and practice Learning outcomes: L02, L03

Wk 3 Tutorial: Conversational Inquiry in Health, Sport Pedagogy and Education Practice Overarching Themes: Explore how conversational inquiry has been used in research and teaching practice across health, sport pedagogy, and education Identify the different purposes, frameworks, and interview approaches used in conversational inquiry Consider how different interview and conversational approaches shape what people are invited to share, how they share it, and what might remain unspoken Practise developing open-ended conversational prompts related to a topic of interest in teaching, learning, health, sport pedagogy, or education, and use peer feedback to refine these prompts Reflect on their own positionality, as well as the ethical and relational responsibilities involved in conducting conversational inquiry Practise seeking, providing, and applying constructive feedback as part of developing a more thoughtful, ethical, and responsive conversational inquiry approach Learning outcomes: L02, L03, L04

Wk 4 Lecture: Qualitative Unobtrusive Inquiry - Learning from Documents, Artefacts and Existing Materials Overarching Themes: Explain why researchers and teaching professionals use unobtrusive inquiry in health, sport pedagogy and education Understand how unobtrusive inquiry can be used to study documents, policies, curricula, media, online content, archives and other existing materials Identify common forms of unobtrusive inquiry, such as literature reviews, scoping reviews, content analysis, critical discourse analysis and archival research Recognise how different frameworks shape what researchers notice, analyse and interpret in documents, artefacts and existing materials Explain how unobtrusive inquiry can support research, professional learning, curriculum development and teaching practice Learning outcomes: L03

Wk 4 Tutorial: Reviewing and Analysing Texts in Health, Sport Pedagogy and Education Overarching Themes: Explain how reviews can help researchers and teaching professionals understand what is already known about a topic Identify different types of reviews, such as literature reviews and scoping reviews, and describe what they are used for Explore how discourse analysis can be used to examine the language, ideas and assumptions in policies, curricula, media or professional texts Practise making basic observations about patterns, gaps, silences or assumptions in a set of texts, and use peer feedback to refine these observations Discuss how reviews and discourse analysis can inform research, professional learning and teaching practice Practise seeking, providing and applying constructive feedback on their interpretations of texts and how they use analysis to inform research, professional learning and teaching practice Learning outcomes: L01, L03, L04

Wk 5 Lecture: Qualitative Field Inquiry - Studying Practice in Real-World Settings Overarching Themes: Explain why researchers and teaching professionals study health, sport pedagogy and education in real-world settings Understand how field inquiry can help researchers examine people, practices, relationships, cultures and contexts Identify common forms of field inquiry, such as ethnography, case studies, observations and field-based inquiry Recognise how different frameworks (e.g. positivist, constructivist, Aboriginal/ Indigenous paradigms) shape what researchers notice, record and interpret in field-based research Explain how field inquiry can produce knowledge that is useful for research, professional learning and teaching practice Learning outcomes: L03

Wk 5 Tutorial: Using Practitioner Enquiry to Improve Health, Sport Pedagogy and Educational Practice Overarching Theme: Explain how practitioner enquiry can help teaching professionals investigate and improve their own practice Identify a practical issue, question or area of curiosity from health, sport pedagogy and education practice Consider what kinds of evidence teaching and pedagogy professionals might collect from their own practice, such as observations, reflections, student work, lesson materials or conversations Discuss how practitioner enquiry can support professional learning, curriculum development and pedagogical change Reflect on the ethical responsibilities involved when teaching professionals research their own practice
Wk 6 Lecture: AT1 - Reading and Interpreting Qualitative Research In-Class Assessment. Learning outcomes: L03, L05

Wk 6 Tutorial: Quantitative Descriptive and Correlational Research - Describing Patterns and Relationships in Research Overarching Themes: Explain how descriptive research can help researchers and teaching professionals understand what is happening in health, sport pedagogy and education Explain how correlational research can help researchers and teaching professionals examine relationships between different factors Identify the kinds of questions descriptive and correlational research can help answer Interpret basic descriptive and correlational findings in descriptive research published by a professional organisation in the field Discuss how descriptive and correlational research can inform professional learning, decision-making and teaching practice Learning outcomes: L01, L02, L03, L06

Wk 7 Lecture: Quantitative Quasi-Experimental Research - Studying Change in Real-World Health, Sport Pedagogy and Education Settings Overarching Themes: Explain why researchers and teaching professionals use quasi-experimental research in health, sport pedagogy and education Understand how quasi-experimental research can be used to study change, impact or improvement in real-world settings Identify common features of quasi-experimental research, such as comparison groups, pre- and post-testing, interventions and naturally occurring groups Recognise how quasi-experimental research differs from fully experimental research Discuss what quasi-experimental research can and cannot claim about whether something “works” Learning outcomes: L03

Wk 7 Tutorial: Understanding Whether Something Works in Health, Sport Pedagogy and Education Practice Overarching Themes: Identify the purpose, design and key features of a quasi-experimental study Explain what change or impact a quasi-experimental study is trying to examine Interpret basic findings from a quasi-experimental study in health, sport pedagogy and education Discuss the strengths and limitations of using quasi-experimental research in real-world teaching and learning settings Consider how quasi-experimental research can inform professional decision-making, programme improvement and teaching practice Learning outcomes: L01, L03
Wk 8 Lecture: AT2 - Reading and Interpreting Quantitative Research In-class assessment task. Learning outcomes: L03, L05

Wk 8 Tutorial: Synthesising Research and Developing a Study Purpose Overarching Theme: Organise selected research articles around a topic of interest in health, sport pedagogy and education Compare findings across different studies to identify patterns, extensions, tensions and possibilities Begin critically synthesising the selected literature into a clear account of what is known and what could be explored Develop a purpose statement for a potential study based on the selected literature Draft specific research question(s) that connect to the literature, purpose and possible research design Learning outcomes: L01, L02, L05

Wk 9 Lecture: Choosing a Research Design Responsibly Overarching Themes: Explain how researchers and teaching professionals choose a research design based on a study purpose and research question(s) Revisit common research designs, such as conversational inquiry, field inquiry, unobtrusive inquiry, descriptive research, correlational research and quasi-experimental research Explain why some research designs are better suited to particular purposes and research question(s) than others Understand the ethical responsibilities involved in planning research with people, practices, documents, data or communities Recognise the role of self-reflection and reflexivity in making thoughtful and ethical research decisions Learning outcomes: L03

Wk 9 Tutorial: Designing an Ethical Study Overarching Themes: Review the purpose statement and research question(s) developed from their selected literature Consider which research design is most appropriate for their study purpose and research question(s) Explain why their chosen design is suitable for what they want to understand, explore, describe, examine or evaluate Identify key ethical issues that may need to be considered in their proposed study, including how they might consult with relevant community members, participants or professional stakeholders in respectful and meaningful ways Reflect on how their own assumptions, experiences, values and professional position may shape the way they design the study Consider how consultation with community members, participants or professional stakeholders can strengthen the ethical, relational and practical relevance of their proposed study Learning outcomes: L01, L02, L05

Wk 10 Lec/Tut: Pitching Your Research Proposal Overarching Themes: Present a draft research proposal that identifies a research purpose, research question(s), framework, design, ethical considerations, positionality and potential implications for professional practice Explain how their proposed study is justified by the literature they have reviewed Explain why their chosen framework and research design are suited to the purpose and research question(s) of the proposed study Reflect on how their own position, experiences, values and professional context shape the study and its ethical responsibilities Discuss how the proposed study may inform, challenge or improve professional teaching practice Practise giving, receiving and applying constructive feedback on the clarity, coherence, justification, ethics and professional significance of proposed studies Learning outcomes: L02, L04, L05, L06
